question: Gol Gumbaz is the mausoleum of the king Mohammed Adil Shah. It is a part of _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bijapur.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gol Gumbaz is a 17th-century mausoleum located in Bijapur, a city in Karnataka, India.**
 
• It is the** tomb of Mohammad Adil Shah and houses his mortal remains.**
 
• The mausoleum is **notable for its scale and exceptionally large dome.**
 
• The building is on** UNESCO's "tentative list" **to become a **World Heritage Site in 2014.**
 
• It is the** second-largest dome ever built, **next in size only to St Peter’s Basilica in Rome.
 
• A particular attraction in this monument is the** central chamber, where every sound is echoed seven times.**
 
• Another attraction at the Gol Gumbaz is the** Whispering Gallery, where even minute sounds can be heard clearly 37 meters away.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohammed Adil Shah**

 
 
• ​Mohammed Adil Shah was the** son of Ibrahim Adil Shah II.**
 
• He was the **seventh ruler of Bijapur, **crowned in 1627 at the age of 15 years.
 
• He assisted the Mughals with their campaigns against the Ahmednagar Sultanate. 
 
• He signed a** peace treaty with the Mughals in 1636.**
 
• Kingdom attained its dominions** stretched from the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal.**
 
• Bijapur also attained peace and prosperity during Mohammed’s reign.
 
• His kingdom yielded an **annual revenue of seven crores and eighty-four lakh rupees.**
 
• He** died in 1656 and was buried in the Gol Gumbaz.**
